disclaimer.paragraph1: Clap is a financial technology company and is not a bank. Banking, payment processing, and other regulated financial services are provided through licensed financial institution and payment partners.
disclaimer.paragraph2: Clap provides technology that enables users to exchange supported currencies, initiate cross-border transfers, and make payments through supported financial networks.
disclaimer.paragraph3: Currency exchange, payment processing, settlement, and payout services are facilitated by third-party financial institutions and payment partners.
disclaimer.paragraph4: Products and services may vary by country and are subject to eligibility requirements, regulatory approvals, identity verification, compliance checks, and transaction limits.

FAQ.title: Frequently asked questions
FAQ.description: Learn how Clap makes exchanging currencies and sending money across African borders simpler.

q1.question: What is Clap?
q1.answer: Clap is a cross-border payments platform that makes it easier for individuals and businesses to exchange currencies and send money between countries. We're starting by connecting Nigeria and Benin Republic, making transactions between Naira and CFA simpler and more accessible.

q2.question: Which currencies does Clap support?
q2.answer: Clap is starting with the Nigerian Naira (NGN) and West African CFA Franc (XOF). Users will be able to exchange between these currencies and send money across supported payment networks.

q3.question: How do cross-border transfers work?
q3.answer: Simply enter the amount you want to exchange, review the available exchange rate and the amount your recipient will receive, provide their payment details, and confirm your transaction. Payouts are made through supported bank and mobile money networks.

q4.question: Are there hidden charges?
q4.answer: Clap is built around transparent pricing. You'll be able to review the applicable exchange rate, fees, and final payout amount before confirming a transaction.

q5.question: Is Clap a bank?
q5.answer: No. Clap is a financial technology company, not a bank. Regulated financial services, including payment processing and settlement, are facilitated through licensed third-party financial institution and payment partners.

q6.question: When can I start using Clap?
q6.answer: Clap is preparing for early access. Join our waitlist and we'll notify you as soon as the platform is ready.
